## Your task — root-cause the first-run large-library initial-sync hang
Symptom: users with a LARGE existing Apple Health library experience a hang/stall during the initial sync at first run — exactly at the first-run/purchase moment, which costs App Store ratings.

Work in /Users/example/Projects/products/exampleapp — the iOS app lives under ios_app/. STRICTLY READ-ONLY: never write, edit, or create any file in that repo; do not build or run it; do not touch ~/.compound; no external/network actions. Static analysis only (Read/Grep/Glob).

1. Locate the first-run initial HealthKit sync implementation (onboarding → first sync path).
2. Identify the root cause of the hang with concrete file:line evidence — e.g. unbatched full-library anchored/sample queries, synchronous main-thread waits, unbounded memory accumulation, missing pagination/limits, serial per-type fetches, blocking UI on completion of the entire library.
3. Name ONE bounded fix (smallest change that removes the first-run hang) plus its verification plan. Not a rewrite.

content.text:
ROOT CAUSE: The local "Full Archive" health-data export path reads each HealthKit type with a single unbounded `HKSampleQuery(limit: HKObjectQueryNoLimit)` over a 10-year range and accumulates every sample into one in-memory `[ExportRow]` array (then globally sorts it) — for a large library this is a hundreds-of-MB allocation spike that jetsam-kills or freezes the app, and it is Pro-gated so it fires immediately after the first-run purchase.

MECHANISM: A large-library user finishes onboarding, selects Full Archive (10 years), and taps Export. That range is Pro-gated, so they hit the paywall, purchase, and the export runs. `fetchDiscreteExportData` issues one `HKSampleQuery` with `limit: HKObjectQueryNoLimit` and a date-sorted descriptor per discrete metric; HealthKit materializes the entire matched set (heart rate alone on a multi-year Apple Watch user is commonly 500K–2M+ `HKQuantitySample` objects, each carrying source/device metadata) into a single array delivered in one callback. Each sample is then `compactMap`-copied into an `ExportRow`, multiple metrics accumulate into one `rows` array, and `fetchExportData` finishes with `rows.sorted { $0.date < $1.date }` over the whole combined set. Peak simultaneous memory (raw HKSample array + parallel ExportRow copy + sort) blows past the app's jetsam budget; the export spinner (`isExporting`) never resolves and iOS terminates the app — the "hang/stall" right after purchase. Notably the server SYNC path was already refactored (v1.6.6) to page reads at 10K/loop specifically to avoid this exact OOM; the local EXPORT path never received that treatment.

EVIDENCE:
- `ios_app/Sources/HealthSync/HealthKitManager.swift:648` — `fetchDiscreteExportData`: `HKSampleQuery(..., limit: HKObjectQueryNoLimit, sortDescriptors: [sort])` — unbounded single-shot full-history read, no pagination.
- `ios_app/Sources/HealthSync/HealthKitManager.swift:514` — `fetchExportData` returns `rows.sorted { $0.date < $1.date }` — global in-memory sort of the entire combined sample set.
- `ios_app/Sources/HealthSync/HealthKitManager.swift:696`, `:845`, `:967` — sleep / medication / workout export siblings, all `HKObjectQueryNoLimit`, same unbounded pattern.
- `ios_app/Sources/HealthSync/ExportView.swift:604` + `:624` — Full Archive preset = 10 years (`byAdding: .year, value: -10`), the widest range fed to those queries.
- `ios_app/Sources/HealthSync/ExportView.swift:529` and `:749-752` — CSV/JSON beyond 7 days is Pro-gated → paywall → purchase precedes the export run (the "first-run purchase moment").
- `ios_app/Sources/HealthSync/ExportView.swift:768-813` — the export Task fans `fetchExportData` + sleep/workout/medication fetches, all accumulating into one `rows` array before writing.
- CONTRAST proving this path, not the server sync, is the live hang: `HealthKitExtractor.swift:138-140` (page-size comment: "instead of loading all 790K+ samples at once (~500MB → OOM crash)") and `:168-192` (`fetchQuantitySamplesPage`, `limit: queryPageSize` 10_000); `SyncEngine.swift:2416` (paged quantity stream), `:2114` (paged workout stream), `:2212` (year-windowed cumulative). The sync path is bounded; the export path is not.

BOUNDED FIX: In `ios_app/Sources/HealthSync/HealthKitManager.swift`, replace the unbounded export reads with a windowed/paged read that reuses the pattern already proven in the sync engine — do NOT rewrite the export-to-file pipeline. Concretely: chunk `fetchDiscreteExportData` (and the sleep/workout/medication siblings) by calendar window (reuse `CalendarYearWindowPolicy`, or page via `HKAnchoredObjectQuery` with `limit: HealthKitExtractor.queryPageSize` like `fetchQuantitySamplesPage`), converting each bounded page/window to `ExportRow`s and streaming them into `ExportEngine`'s CSV writer per window instead of building one giant `[ExportRow]` and sorting it globally. Windowing also removes the need for the `rows.sorted` full-set sort (each window is written in order). Smallest viable first cut: apply it to `fetchDiscreteExportData` only — the discrete-quantity path (heart rate) is the dominant sample-count driver; the other siblings can follow the same helper.

VERIFICATION PLAN: Seed a large synthetic HealthKit library (≈1–2M heart-rate samples across 10 years) on a device/sim, sign in as Pro, select Full Archive + heart rate, and export while profiling with Instruments Allocations. Baseline (current): peak memory hits hundreds of MB and the app jetsams / spinner never completes. Post-fix: peak stays bounded (tens of MB, ~one page/window at a time), export completes, and the emitted CSV row count matches the seeded sample count. Add a unit/integration test against a fake reader that returns a large synthetic set and asserts the export fetch never holds more than one page/window of raw samples at once (spy on page-callback count and sizes), mirroring the existing sync tests (`SyncProgressTests`, `LiveHealthQueryCoordinatorTests`).

CONFIDENCE: medium-high. The unbounded-read root cause is proven by file:line and by direct contrast with the already-paged sync path; the only inferential step is mapping the operator's phrase "initial sync" onto the local full-archive EXPORT rather than the server backfill. Falsifier: if a repro shows the large-library freeze on the SERVER sync/backfill path (not export), or if a crash log shows a main-thread watchdog `0x8badf00d` rather than a memory `jetsam`/`0xdead10cc` termination, then the hang is elsewhere (main-thread block) and paging the export read would not resolve it — I found no unbounded read remaining in the server sync path, which is why I rule it out as the current culprit. Secondary latent risk worth flagging, not the primary: `LiveHealthQueryCoordinator` (`LiveHealthQueryCoordinator.swift:237-241`) starts 8 `HKAnchoredObjectQuery`s with `anchor: nil, predicate: nil, limit: HKObjectQueryNoLimit` — a full-library-in-one-callback bomb on first run — but it is kill-switch-gated OFF by default (`Config.liveHealthQueriesEnabled`, `Config.swift:168`), so it is not the shipping hang unless that flag is flipped.

PRODUCT-LOOP TIE-BACK: This closes envelope work_6fa53aab92bb as the bounded diagnosis slice of card work_08712e4b59a0 (fix the large-library initial-sync hang that costs stars at the first-run purchase moment). It directly attacks the card's binding constraint — download/retention velocity — because the failure lands after payment, producing exactly the 1-star reviews that suppress ranking; a paged/windowed export removes the OOM at the moment of highest intent. The finding should register as a new ProductSignal (root-caused defect, file:line evidence) and a testable ProductHypothesis ("paging the export read eliminates the post-purchase jetsam on large libraries") into the exampleapp ProductLoop, whose live doctor is currently ok (signals=4, hypotheses=1); execution of the one bounded fix routes to Codex, not this reasoning lane.

CLAIMS CONSUMED:
- claim_6a6fb980bf59 — used to anchor the product-loop tie-back: framed the diagnosis as a new ProductSignal + ProductHypothesis feeding the exampleapp ProductLoop and referenced its current live doctor state (signals=4, hypotheses=1) as the surface this finding lands into.
